> **Status: Current planning checklist; no release candidate exists.**
> Sub-issue of #304 (study under #303, Phase 7 cluster 2). An exploratory experiment: its results are labelled diagnostics, not gates, release evidence or speed claims. Stage A is complete with qualifications; the Stage B first slice is blocked at its required verifier. CP5/CP6 remain incomplete.

## Goal

Find out **how long real work takes, and what breaks**, when one large real project is used through the mount shape cluster 2 plans — before cluster 2 is built and without waiting for cluster 1.

Product goal behind it: a **full Workspace** (source, `.git`, dependencies, caches, build output) and a **Workspace per bash tool call** for an agent workload.

**Time is the result.** Wall time per phase of each tool call (mount, exec, commit, unmount). No CPU, memory or cgroup telemetry; only counts that come for free.

## The case

`deepseek-harness` at `639ed01539`, the whole checkout, with Node:

| | Files | Directories | Symlinks | Bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full tree | 103,108 | 16,867 | 10,070 | 3.237 GiB |
| Every `node_modules` | 71,893 | 13,086 | 10,042 | 1.980 GiB |
| Tree without `node_modules` | 31,215 | 3,781 | 28 | 1.257 GiB |

No network: the tree is copied once into a Docker volume as a closed master, and the install is a **replay** from that master (copy and hard-link variants), not a run of pnpm.

## Stages

| Stage | Under the command | Explores |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Passthrough FUSE, with the product's mount profile and with a kernel-caching profile | FUSE, mount profile, tool compatibility; the floor |
| B | Prototype of the overlay (four SQLite tables, generation rules) over a local directory as the committed base | Overlay and Workspace |
| C | Stage B plus daemon behaviours: Workspace registry, several Execs, a Workspace per call, capture / install / retire with a stand-in publish | Daemon; per-call cost |

## Owner decision — promote A2, 2026-10-04

The owner has selected the **original cached A2 profile** as the preferred profile for subsequent experiment work and the Phase 7 mount-design candidate. This prospectively supersedes the original §8 selection rule that chose A1 unless A1 failed correctness and A2 passed. It does not change the product implementation or qualify a release.

- **Promoted settings:** 60 s entry/attribute TTL, cached reads / KEEP_CACHE, 128 KiB requests, existing two FUSE threads and background/congestion 1. Kernel writeback remains **off**; writes still reach the daemon. A2 accepts fsync as a no-op without a durability claim and continues to refuse xattrs.
- **A2O and A2P are not promoted.** Narrower locking/stable enumeration did not establish a reliable general speed improvement. The matched readdirplus diagnostic improved E04/E02 observations modestly but regressed E10; it remains a separate diagnostic.
- **Preserve historical evidence:** Stage A receipts and the original A1-based B/E10 FAILED receipt retain their exact profile, identity, numbers and status. A future A2-based overlay slice needs a prospectively frozen new identity and the same required correctness proof. It cannot inherit a passing B result from Stage A or relabel the previous failure.
- **Qualification:** A2 still has material overhead on bulk work and is not proven equivalent to native performance. Cache invalidation for overlay/Commit transitions, bounded memory and concurrency remain to be established. Record runs begin after equal sync + VM drop_caches preconditioning; there is no residency proof, no pre-warming, and no release-admission claim.
- **Current completion:** CP5/CP6 remain incomplete. This decision selects a direction; it does not claim the B verifier blocker is fixed or authorize silently reducing verification scope.

Evidence is in local, unpushed experiment commits `c73dceb75` (original Stage A), `92b414e36` (A2O diagnostic) and `3331ef857` (matched A2P diagnostic), with reports under `core/docs/issues/305/`. See the decision comment for exact observed times.

## Experiments

- **17 tool calls** (E01–E17) on native, both passthrough profiles and the prototype: fixed cost of a call, walking 130,045 names, reading 3.237 GiB, `git status` / log / grep, Node start-up, `tsc -b`, `node --test`, a one-file edit and commit, a 2,007-file branch switch, installing 95,021 entries (two variants), removing them, a 220 MB file, log appends, temporary-file churn.
- **8 daemon scenarios** (C01–C08): a Workspace per call, 100 small Commits, Commit time against change size, Commit during continuous writes, two Workspaces, four Execs, the configured limits, refusal and teardown.

Every run is verified against an oracle from the native arm: same exit code and output, same resulting tree, and for B and C the same tree again after a Commit and a fresh mount.

## Rules

One run per experiment per arm; a declared cold cache state, equal for every arm; setup outside the timers; tests run one by one, each with a **60 s hard stop** (owner direction, 2026-10-03) recorded as `EXCEEDED` together with how far the test got; no workload is shrunk to fit; failures kept in the report. Reporting lines, not gates: 100 ms fixed cost per tool call, 2 × the native arm, 15 s absolute.

## Prerequisites and decisions — resolved 2026-10-03

The owner chose `core/experiment/` for the code, said the handoff agent may install what the experiment needs, and delegated the remaining unblocking decisions. Taken under that delegation; the owner can change any of them:

- [x] **P1.** The handoff agent fetches `node-v24.21.0-linux-arm64.tar.xz` from nodejs.org on the host, once, and verifies its published checksum. If it cannot, the three Node experiments are `NOT_RUN` and the rest proceeds.
- [x] **P2.** SQLite may run inside this experiment's container: a scoped exception recorded at the head of `docs/general/benchmark_rules.md`. The permanent hosting rule and owner question Q2 on #303 are unchanged.
- [x] **Parameters.** Code in `core/experiment/` (its own Cargo workspace, rules in `core/experiment/AGENTS.md`); 2 Workspaces and 4 Execs in the daemon scenarios; one non-root command identity; the prototype capped at 3,000 lines of Rust.
- [x] **Worktree.** Its own worktree, `/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/phase7-experiment-305/layerfs`, on branch `codex/phase7-experiment-305`, created from `7edddbdb8`. All code, runs, reports and commits happen there.

Nothing blocks the start. The handoff prompt is in the first comment.

## Working fast

Smoke runs on a small sealed subset of the tree for development (as many as needed, never reported); record runs on the full tree, once per test per arm. One vertical slice first, then tests one at a time, cheapest first. A record run spoiled by a harness defect is kept as `INVALID` and taken once more under the new build.

## Checkpoints

At every checkpoint: commit on the experiment branch (with the production LOC line, delta 0), tick it here, and post a comment with the result rows so far.

- [x] **CP0** — plan, tree rules and handoff prompt committed (`b26f518de`, local; not pushed); worktree and branch created.
- [x] **CP1** — preparation: master volume and manifest, smoke subset, image, runner and verifier skeleton, oracle.
- [x] **CP2** — first slice: E01 and E04 verified on native and both passthrough profiles.
- [x] **CP3** — stage A complete and reported; mount profile for stage B chosen.
- [x] **CP4** — prototype slice attempted and reported: E01/F verifies; E10/F FAILED at the 10 s mounted-tree proof. A passing slice was not achieved.
- [ ] **CP5** — stage B complete and reported. **Incomplete:** required first slice failed; remaining B selections NOT_RUN.
- [ ] **CP6** — stage C complete and reported. **NOT_RUN:** B E10/E12 prerequisite unmet.
- [x] **CP7** — summary at the real verifier blocker; proposals posted to #303. Full experiment remains incomplete.

## Not covered

Cluster 1 (chunking, packing, MinIO, PostgreSQL, publication), the real cost of base reads, the SDK and control path, native tools in `node_modules`, and CPU or memory behaviour.

Plan: `core/docs/issues/305/EXPERIMENT-PLAN.md`; handoff prompt: `core/docs/issues/305/HANDOFF-PROMPT.md`; tree rules: `core/experiment/AGENTS.md` — committed on `codex/phase7-experiment-305` at `b26f518de` (local). Background, uncommitted in the cluster 2 worktree: `core/docs/issues/304/tough-situations.md` and the #303 plan.


CP1 qualification (d126c2c25, local; not pushed): Preparation reached; E08 has no completed oracle after the required untimed pair hit 60 s; E09 raw stdout is nondeterministic and its record cells remain NOT_RUN. Other native oracles and faithful replay checks are complete. The clean checkpoint source is used to seal the record image next.


CP3 qualification (c73dceb75, local; not pushed): 51 verified record cells (36 OK, 15 SLOW); E09/N/A1/A2 NOT_RUN for nondeterministic raw stdout. All attempted content/cleanup checks pass. Stage B profile is A1 under the plan rule; both replay variants verified.


CP4 qualification (3faebb26e, local; not pushed): Reached as a bad-news checkpoint only: E01/F OK; E10/F FAILED because required mounted-tree verification exceeded 10 s. CP5 and CP6 remain incomplete; first-slice expansion and Stage C prerequisites are unmet.


CP7 qualification (e5fb8a4e5, local; not pushed): Summary/proposals complete at the verifier blocker, not a completed full experiment. CP5/CP6 remain incomplete; B E10 full mounted-tree proof FAILED at 10 s, B E12 and all C scenarios NOT_RUN.

## Handoff prompt

Hand this to the agent that builds and runs the experiment. Source file: `core/docs/issues/305/HANDOFF-PROMPT.md` on branch `codex/phase7-experiment-305` (commit `b26f518de`, local). Updated 2026-10-03: own worktree, 60 s cap per test, fast iteration, and a commit plus an issue update at every checkpoint.

---

You are building and running an **exploratory experiment** for LayerFS. It is not
product work: you write throwaway experiment code, run it, and report what you
measured. The plan is already written and its open parameters are decided.
Follow the plan; do not redesign it. Work fast, in small verified steps, and
publish progress at every checkpoint.

## The situation

LayerFS is a content-addressed, layered filesystem for agent sandboxes. Phase 7
rebuilds its sandbox side ("cluster 2") around a daemon-owned SQLite overlay.
Cluster 2 has not started, and cluster 1 (storage) is being implemented by
someone else. Before cluster 2 is built, the owner wants to know how long real
work takes, and what breaks, when a large real project is used through the mount
shape cluster 2 plans. The product goal is a full Workspace — source, `.git`,
dependencies, caches — and a Workspace per bash tool call for an agent, so
**time is the result that matters**.

## Where you work

- **Worktree:** `/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/phase7-experiment-305/layerfs`
- **Branch:** `codex/phase7-experiment-305`, created from `7edddbdb8`.

Work only there. Its Cargo target directory and its measurement lock are its
own. Do not build, run or write in any other worktree.

## Where to read, in this order

In your worktree:

1. `core/docs/issues/305/EXPERIMENT-PLAN.md` — **the plan you execute**: the
   case, the arms, the 17 tool calls and 8 daemon scenarios, the verification,
   the measurement rules, the decided parameters, the fast-iteration rules (§11)
   and the checkpoints (§12).
2. `core/experiment/AGENTS.md` — the rules for the tree you write code in.
3. `AGENTS.md` (repository root) and `core/AGENTS.md` — measurement and source
   rules. They bind you.
4. `core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs` and `adapter.rs` — the product's
   mount profile, which the passthrough must copy.

Background, uncommitted in the cluster 2 worktree; read at these absolute paths
and change none of them:

5. `/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/phase7-cluster2-sandbox/layerfs/core/docs/issues/304/tough-situations.md`
   — why each test exists, and the measured shape of the example tree.
6. The same folder's `mount.md`, `exec.md`, `commit.md` and `fuse.md` — the
   cluster 2 design the stage B and C prototype imitates.
7. `/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/phase7-cluster2-sandbox/layerfs/core/docs/issues/303/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`
   — reference only: §0.3 (tables), §0.4 (ordering), §0.5 (paths) and decision
   D4 (SQLite settings).

The example tree is `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/deepseek-harness` at commit
`639ed01539`. **Never run a command in it or write to it.** Copy it once into a
Docker volume and work on copies of that.

## What is already decided — do not reopen

- Code lives in `core/experiment/`, as its own Cargo workspace.
- Rust with `fuser` 0.18.0 for the mount and `rusqlite` 0.40.2 for the overlay
  prototype; Python 3 standard library for the runner, replayer and verifier.
- The install is a **replay** from the master copy, in a copy variant and a
  hard-link variant. No pnpm, no network.
- You may fetch one file on the host: `node-v24.21.0-linux-arm64.tar.xz` from
  `nodejs.org/dist/v24.21.0/`, verified against that directory's
  `SHASUMS256.txt`. Nothing else is downloaded or pulled. If it cannot be
  fetched, record E07–E09 as `NOT_RUN` and continue.
- SQLite may run inside the experiment's container. This is a scoped exception
  for this experiment, recorded at the head of `docs/general/benchmark_rules.md`.
- **Tests run one by one, each with a hard stop of 60 s; the aim is to finish
  far sooner.** Reporting lines: 100 ms fixed cost per tool call, 2 × the native
  arm, 15 s absolute.
- Limits for the daemon scenarios: 2 Workspaces, 4 Execs. One non-root command
  identity, uid and gid 1000.
- The prototype is capped at 3,000 physical lines of Rust.

## Work fast

The plan's §11 is the rule; this is how to apply it.

- **Two modes.** *Smoke* runs use a small sealed subset of the tree, skip the
  cache drop, and are for development: run them as often as you like, discard
  their output, never report them. *Record* runs use the full tree under the
  measurement rules and are taken once.
- **Get a number early.** First make one test (E01, then E04) pass end to end on
  native and both passthrough profiles. Post those rows. Only then add the next
  test. Do not write all seventeen tests before running one.
- **Cheapest first, install last.** Add tests one at a time in rising cost. The
  95,021-entry install replay is the last thing you build in each stage.
- **Make the loop short.** The runner takes one test, one arm and one mode per
  invocation. Build incrementally and bind-mount the binary into a long-lived
  development container; build the sealed image only for record runs. A smoke
  pass of a single test should take seconds.
- **Never debug on the full tree.** If a record run exposes a defect, fix it
  against the smoke subset, then take the record run once under the new build.
- **Do not polish.** The code is throwaway. Prefer the shortest thing that
  measures correctly over structure, options or abstractions. Do not build
  features the plan does not list.
- **Keep moving.** Do not wait for review between checkpoints. Stop only for a
  real blocker, and say exactly what it is and what you tried.

## Checkpoints: commit and update the issue at every one

The plan's §12 lists them (CP1 preparation, CP2 first slice, CP3 stage A, CP4
prototype slice, CP5 stage B, CP6 stage C, CP7 summary; CP0 is done). At each:

1. **Commit** on `codex/phase7-experiment-305`. The message must carry
   `Production LOC: <before> -> <after> (delta 0)` and the method —
   `python3 tools/production_loc.py --root <tree>` on the first parent and on the
   staged tree. At the base the counter reports core 70,279, reference 65,417,
   combined 135,696; your commits must leave it unchanged. Do not push unless
   the owner asks.
2. **Update issue #305**: tick the checkpoint in the body and post one comment
   containing what was done, the result rows so far (status and time per phase),
   every failed, exceeded, invalid or unrun row with its cause, the commit hash,
   and the next step. Keep it short; a table and a few lines.
3. **Continue** to the next checkpoint.

A checkpoint with bad news is still a checkpoint: commit and report it.

## What makes this hard

- **The measurement rules are strict and they are not optional.** One record run
  per test per arm. No repeat to check, to average or to replace a number you
  dislike. The cache state is declared and identical in every arm. Setup stays
  outside the timers. A failed or slow row is a finding; keep it.
- **The 60 s cap will be hit.** Several full-tree tests will probably reach it.
  That is expected and useful. A test that reaches it is recorded `EXCEEDED` and
  is not rerun; never shrink a workload or raise the cap to make it finish. Make
  every long-running test able to say how far it got when stopped — entries
  created, bytes moved, names walked, calls completed.
- **A result that is fast but wrong is `FAILED`.** Verify every record run
  against the oracle before reading its time.
- **The oracle must be deterministic.** Fix git identity and dates. Find the
  output files that differ between two native runs and exclude them by name
  before any timed run, not after.
- **The mount profile must be the product's.** Copy the mount options and the
  capability negotiation from the product adapter. A passthrough with a
  different profile measures something else.
- **The prototype must stay small.** It imitates the planned rules well enough
  to time them. It is not the product, it implements no cluster 1 work, and its
  publish step is a stand-in. If you approach the line cap, stop and report.
- **The base in stages B and C is a local directory.** Its read cost says
  nothing about PostgreSQL or MinIO. Do not present it as if it did.
- **The tree's native binaries are Darwin builds.** Only pure-JavaScript tools
  run in the Linux container. Do not try to make vitest, tsdown or oxlint work.

## Constraints

- Change nothing under `core/crates/`. No product code, no test of product code.
- Use only crates already in the repository lockfiles and the local Cargo
  registry; build `--locked` and offline. Do not patch or vendor anything.
- Do not touch cluster 1's work or its containers, and do not interrupt another
  owner's run. Two record runs in your worktree never overlap, and nothing else
  heavy runs during one.
- Raw receipts go under `benchmark-results/experiment/`, a fresh path per run.
  That directory is ignored by git; what must survive goes into the reports.
- Do not invent numbers. Report what was measured, with its identity; mark
  anything you could not establish as unknown.

## What to hand back

In `core/docs/issues/305/`, one report per stage and a summary, each with the
repository's status banner:

- per test and arm: status, time per phase, time relative to the native arm,
  which reporting lines it crosses, and the free counts;
- every `SLOW`, `EXCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `INVALID` and `NOT_RUN` row with its cause,
  and for an exceeded test how far it got;
- the identities the plan lists, and the exact reproduction commands;
- in the summary: what works well, what remains a challenge, the decision each
  finding informs, and proposed changes to the #303 plan as proposals for the
  owner.

Keep each report as short as completeness allows, and say plainly what you
verified and what you did not.

## Checkpoint CP0 — plan committed

- **Worktree:** `/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/phase7-experiment-305/layerfs`, branch `codex/phase7-experiment-305`, from `7edddbdb8`.
- **Commit:** `b26f518de` (local; not pushed). Four files: the experiment plan, the handoff prompt, `core/experiment/AGENTS.md`, and the scoped exception in `docs/general/benchmark_rules.md`.
- **Production LOC:** 135696 -> 135696 (delta 0); core 70279, reference 65417. Method: `python3 tools/production_loc.py --root <tree>` on the first parent and on the staged tree.
- **Checks run:** `core/tools/check_product_boundary.py` PASS (357 files); the tool self-tests, 9 OK. Cargo test, clippy and fmt were not run: no Rust source changed.
- **Results:** none. No experiment code exists and nothing has been run.
- **Changed since the issue was opened:** hard stop 60 s per test (was 600 s), tests one by one; smoke and record modes; checkpoints CP0–CP7 with a commit and an issue update at each.
- **Next:** CP1, preparation — master volume and manifest, smoke subset, image, runner and verifier skeleton, oracle.

CP1 preparation reached, with qualifications; commit `d126c2c25b7b82fead704248c3f120c69beed150` (local, not pushed).

- Master copy matches all planned counts; sealed manifest SHA256 `98fd26440b9087bcfd5c23bec9e5497434a2dcb9a27fc85ad0b823ba9c516658`. F/S copies and a sealed small smoke fixture exist in experiment-owned Docker volumes. Linux Node v24.21.0 was downloaded once and checksum-verified. E09 succeeds but raw stdout embeds variable test durations, so its record cells are NOT_RUN under the frozen oracle rule.

Next: seal the local record image from this clean source; take E01 (F/S), then E04, once on N/A1/A2, and post CP2 rows. Full details: `core/docs/issues/305/PREPARATION-REPORT.md`.

| E04 git status | 1.886448751 | 1.917895043 | 3.344448835 | 2.767226876 | −17.259% | 15.5 µs | 1.47 |
| E08 TypeScript build | 71.535252575 (SLOW) | 93.304772710 (SLOW) | 73.339195408 (SLOW) | 99.090949754 (SLOW) | +35.113% | — | 1.39 |

Request counts are identical between A2S and A2S1. The per-request cost in this VM is placement, as the round-trip diagnostic said; the build pays for it (native alone loses 21.8 s on one CPU). The contract's serial estimates were too high on E02 and E14 and wrong in direction on E04. E14/N1 is 27.3% faster than E14/N, one observation, not explained. Host walls of the four E08 cells (95.24–121.96 s) exceed 25 s. A fixed pin is a harness setting, not a product policy. Not answerable here: how much of the cost exists on a Linux host that is not this Docker Desktop VM; the pipe half of `roundtrip_diag.py` needs no FUSE and can be run on a target host.

**A2SL** = A2S answering a LOOKUP of a missing name with node 0 and the 60 s entry lifetime. Four records; E12 SLOW on every FUSE arm.

| Case | N total s | A2WN total s | A2S total s | A2SL total s | A2SL vs A2S | Counted requests A2WN → A2S → A2SL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| E12 copy install | 11.611614797 | 33.788259766 (SLOW) | 32.569615181 (SLOW) | 27.339877844 (SLOW) | −16.057% | 676,038 → 604,146 → 460,360 |

Counts are exactly those declared before the records. The cause is confirmed by smoke count: `shutil.copyfile` to a missing name sends three lookups and A2SL sends one. E12/A2WN was 41.381 s in the `a2-noperm-v1` window with the same requests; windows are not comparable with each other. Host walls of all four cells (25.36–47.98 s) exceed 25 s.

**A2S, A2S1 and A2SL enforce no permissions inside the mount**, as A2WN (SMOKE: a mode-000 file is readable). They are cost measurements, not product candidates. With `default_permissions` the kernel would check the mode at open without a request; that pairing is not measured. Other declared limits: descriptors opened read-write by a root daemon; the lifetime rule releases on the first FORGET and does not track lookup counts; removed directories and symlinks are not kept; hard-link aliasing unqualified; a name created outside the mount stays invisible for up to 60 s on A2SL. Trust probes were not rerun.

Declared interference: shared Docker VM; three other owners' containers present at 0–1.9% CPU at the checks before and after each window; overlap with a timed phase unknown.

Reports: `core/docs/issues/305/A2-{STATELESS,PIN,NEGLOOKUP}-{CONTRACT,REPORT}.md` with their `RECEIPTS` and smoke-count JSON. Prototype 2,771 Rust lines. Experiment build, Clippy, rustfmt, Python and smoke checks pass; product source unchanged and product checks not run. Each commit: production LOC 135696 → 135696 (delta 0), core 70279 / reference 65417, exact parent/staged counter method.

Proposals, not adopted: handle-free regular files and cacheable negative entries for the Phase 7 mount candidate; no handle from CREATE on a no-open mount; treat request placement as the largest remaining lever for metadata-heavy tool calls and measure the pipe round trip on a target Linux host before designing for it. Next, with the owner's go-ahead: a two-mount case for stat identity across mounts.

Stat identity across mounts complete, with the owner's go-ahead for an eighteenth case; local commits `b6660f2d9` (frozen contract `a2-identity-v1`, case E18 and code) and `90d625fc7` (report), not pushed. Earlier evidence and the B failure are unchanged; CP5/CP6 remain incomplete.

**E18** = the frozen E04 command (`git -c core.fsmonitor=false status --porcelain=v1`) after an untimed first run of it in an earlier mount of the same arm. That mount is removed, then `sync` + VM drop_caches=3, then the timers; only the tree on disk, including the refreshed `.git/index`, crosses. It is the tool call that follows an earlier one in a Workspace-per-call model. **A2SI** = A2S with the backing file's inode number as node id instead of a first-touch counter; the daemon persists nothing. Seven records in the frozen order, one per cell, all verified OK, each verifier <10 s, cleanup passes. Diagnostics only, no residency proof.

| Case | N total s | A2 total s | A2S total s | A2SI total s | A2SI vs A2S | Counted requests A2S → A2SI | READ A2S → A2SI | A2SI / N |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| E18 git status, second mount | 0.078895416 | 4.403938252 | 3.555238501 | 0.577977167 | −83.743% | 38,294 → 21,158 | 15,159 → 37 | 7.33 |
| E04 git status, first mount after a copy | 1.966743960 | — | 3.647849251 | 3.773572376 | +3.447% | 38,401 → 38,390 | 15,260 → 15,250 | 1.92 |

The controls have the problem at full scale: in the second mount A2 sends 80,057 requests and A2S reads every tracked file again (14,075 descriptors opened), the same as in their first mount. The contract declined to predict the A2S cell because the smoke tree repeated its numbering by luck (9 reads); the full tree did not. A2SI reads 37 blocks, opens 16 files and does not rewrite the index. E04 is unchanged in count, as it must be: nothing can match after a fresh copy. Its +3.4% comes with identical requests and is one observation. Host walls E18/A2 27.34 s and E18/A2S 25.62 s exceed 25 s; no budget PASS claimed.

What is left on E18/A2SI: 16,876 lookups (one `lstat` per tracked file and directory on a fresh mount) and 4,232 readdirplus; 0.385 s of its 0.540 s Exec is inside the daemon's callbacks. Native answers the same from its inode cache in 0.079 s.

SMOKE count: 254 of 254 tracked files keep their inode number across two mounts on A2SI, 3 of 254 on A2 and A2S; the other fields Git compares are equal on every arm.

**A2SI enforces no permissions**, as A2S, and is a cost measurement. It borrows identity from a backing directory, which an overlay does not have. No generation numbers: a backing inode number reused while the kernel still holds the old inode is unhandled for directories and symlinks. Inode number and ctime both come from the backing file, so they were not separated. Not measured: a tree in which some files changed between the two mounts (next, with the owner's go-ahead), or A2SI combined with negative entries or one-CPU placement.

Declared interference: shared Docker VM; three other owners' containers present at 0–0.9% CPU at the checks before and after the window.

Reports: `core/docs/issues/305/A2-IDENTITY-{CONTRACT,REPORT}.md`, `A2-IDENTITY-{RECEIPTS,SMOKE-COUNTS,RUNNER-SMOKE}.json`. The case list has eighteen cases; E01–E17 are unchanged. Prototype 2,816 Rust lines. Experiment build, Clippy, rustfmt, Python and smoke checks pass; product source unchanged and product checks not run. Each commit: production LOC 135696 → 135696 (delta 0), core 70279 / reference 65417, exact parent/staged counter method.

Proposals, not adopted: an unchanged file must report the same inode number and ctime in every Workspace that contains it; the Workspace must persist `.git/index` after a command that looks read-only; an overlay needs a stored or derived number per file that survives Commit and a new mount.
